verdict.rationale: Morph's own docs describe running production agents and Claude Code on its open-weight models (Kimi K3) through native OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic Messages endpoints, which implies tool-calling agent loops work. However, the pack never explicitly documents function/tool-calling support, its fidelity, or parallel or multi-step tool use. missing for 10: explicit tool-calling documentation, parallel tool call support, multi-step tool loop guarantees, independent or hands-on evidence of faithful tool calling on open models.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on faithful function/tool calling — including parallel and multi-step tool use — so agent loops run on open models without breaking

citations.quote: Move a production agent off Anthropic or OpenAI onto Kimi K3 — a 5% traffic trial or a full migration, gated by Reflexes.
Claude Code speaks the Anthropic Messages API, which Morph serves natively at `/v1/messages`.
Kimi K3 serves 1M context through the standard chat completions endpoint, so existing OpenAI code only needs a new `model` string
Anthropic Messages supports the same open source chat models, token billing, and rate limits.
